cards.definition: A collection of rows and columns holding data about one subject. Formally a relation or entity.
cards.useCase: Keep each kind of thing (customers, products) in its own table so each fact is stored once.

cards.definition: One named field of a table with a single datatype. Formally an attribute.
cards.useCase: Every value in the column must fit its type.

cards.definition: One record in a table, with exactly one value for each column. Formally a tuple.
cards.useCase: Row order carries no meaning, so never rely on it.

cards.definition: The same fact stored in more than one place, which risks the copies disagreeing.
cards.useCase: Avoid it by giving each subject its own table and relating tables with keys.
cards.example: One customer table, referenced by orders

cards.definition: Relational database management system: software that stores data in related tables and retrieves it with SQL.
cards.useCase: Use one when data needs integrity, relationships and multi-user access.

cards.definition: A column, or set of columns, that uniquely identifies each row. It must be unique and never NULL.
cards.useCase: Every table needs one. Keep it compact.

cards.definition: A column whose values refer to the primary key of another table, relating the rows of the two tables.
cards.useCase: Store the customer a purchase belongs to without copying the customer's details.

cards.definition: A primary key made of more than one column, needed when only the combination is unique.
cards.useCase: Use it for rows such as enrolments or order lines.

cards.definition: The table whose primary key a foreign key points to. Also called the primary table.
cards.useCase: Identify which side of a relationship holds the PK.

cards.definition: The table that contains the foreign key. Also called the foreign table.
cards.useCase: Identify which side of a relationship holds the FK.

cards.definition: A marker meaning no value is stored. A primary key can never be NULL.
cards.useCase: Allow it only in columns where a value may legitimately be missing.

cards.definition: A structure that relates each indexed value to where its rows are stored, so lookups are fast, like a book's index.
cards.useCase: Add one on columns you search often. Queries are written the same either way.

cards.definition: A virtual table whose rows are computed from base tables each time it is used. It holds no data itself.
cards.useCase: Give users a simplified or restricted picture of the data.
cards.example:
CREATE VIEW active_patron AS
  SELECT * FROM patron WHERE is_active = 1;

cards.definition: A table that actually stores data, as opposed to a view.
cards.useCase: Tell stored data apart from computed results.

cards.definition: A named routine saved inside the database that can take parameters and run queries or other tasks.
cards.useCase: Reuse one piece of logic, such as customers who spent more than an amount you pass in.

cards.definition: A special stored procedure that fires automatically when data in its table is inserted, updated or deleted.
cards.useCase: Enforce business rules, such as writing an audit record whenever a row is deleted.
cards.example: AFTER DELETE ON staff ... INSERT INTO audit ...

cards.topic: SQL Queries and the System Catalog
cards.definition: The statement that retrieves data. The list after it chooses the columns.
cards.useCase: Read data without changing it.

cards.topic: SQL Queries and the System Catalog
cards.definition: A restriction that keeps only the rows meeting a condition.
cards.useCase: Filter rows; the column list chooses columns, WHERE chooses rows.
cards.example: SELECT title FROM book WHERE price > 15;

cards.topic: SQL Queries and the System Catalog
cards.definition: Links rows from two or more tables by comparing key columns and returning the matching rows. The tables themselves are unchanged.
cards.useCase: Combine data across a relationship, matching an FK with its PK.

cards.topic: SQL Queries and the System Catalog
cards.definition: The statements that add rows, change existing rows, and remove rows.
cards.useCase: Modify data; SELECT only reads it.

cards.topic: SQL Queries and the System Catalog
cards.definition: Statements that build or remove database objects such as tables and views.
cards.useCase: Define or remove structure rather than data.

cards.topic: SQL Queries and the System Catalog
cards.definition: Special system tables, also called the data dictionary, that hold information about the database itself.
cards.useCase: Look up what tables, columns and users exist. Read it; never alter it directly.

cards.topic: SQL Queries and the System Catalog
cards.definition: Data about data, such as a table's column names and types.
cards.useCase: Distinguish descriptions of the data from the data itself.

cards.definition: The contract that tells MySQL how to interpret stored bits, how much space to use, and which operations are valid.
cards.useCase: Pick the smallest, most specific type that represents the data faithfully.

cards.definition: Integers of 1, 2 and 3 bytes. TINYINT covers -128 to 127 (0 to 255 unsigned).
cards.useCase: Use the smallest that fits to save space and keep indexes lean.

cards.definition: A 4-byte integer, about plus or minus 2.1 billion. The default integer.
cards.useCase: General counters and IDs.

cards.definition: An 8-byte integer, about plus or minus 9.2 quintillion.
cards.useCase: IDs or counters that may pass 2 billion.

cards.definition: An attribute that forbids negative values, doubling the positive range.
cards.useCase: Use it when a value can never be negative.

cards.definition: Exact fixed-point number with M total digits and D after the point. No rounding error.
cards.useCase: Money.

cards.definition: Approximate floating-point numbers of 4 and 8 bytes. Fast but imprecise.
cards.useCase: Scientific measurements. Avoid for currency, since 0.1 + 0.2 may not equal 0.3.

cards.definition: A true/false value stored in one byte as 1 or 0.
cards.useCase: On/off flags.

cards.definition: A fixed-length string padded to N characters.
cards.useCase: Uniform values such as two-letter state codes.

cards.definition: A variable-length string of up to N characters (65,535 bytes at most). The default for most text.
cards.useCase: Names, emails and other text of varying length.

cards.definition: Variable-length text from TINYTEXT up to LONGTEXT (255 bytes to 4 GB). Indexes poorly.
cards.useCase: Only when content may exceed VARCHAR limits.

cards.definition: Binary large objects: raw bytes for images and files.
cards.useCase: Store binary content in the database.

cards.definition: One value from a fixed list. Compact and self-validating, but painful to change later.
cards.useCase: A known, stable set of choices.

cards.definition: Zero or more values from a predefined list.
cards.useCase: Several choices at once, such as days a class meets.

cards.definition: DATE holds YYYY-MM-DD (years 1000-9999). TIME holds HH:MM:SS and can exceed 24 hours.
cards.useCase: Calendar dates; clock times or elapsed durations.

cards.definition: A date and time stored as written, with no time zone conversion and a wide range.
cards.useCase: Predictable literal timestamps and dates beyond 2038.

cards.definition: A 4-byte date and time stored as UTC and converted to the session time zone. Limited to 1970-2038.
cards.useCase: Row creation or change times that follow the viewer's time zone.

cards.definition: A one-byte value that holds a year only.
cards.useCase: A model year or graduation year.

cards.definition: A native type for structured documents, with validation and path-based queries.
cards.useCase: Flexible, semi-structured data. Not where a relational column would do.
